title: Cebu Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Edition Was Like
seo_title: Cebu Marathon 2027 Review | The 2026 Edition, Cebu City
meta_description: Cebu Marathon review: 11,529 runners from 47 countries on 11 January 2026, strong results, and hours-long queues for medals that runners loudly criticised.
dek: The Cebu Marathon drew 11,529 runners from 47 countries in January 2026. The racing was strong, but many finishers queued for hours for their medals. Here is what the 18th edition was like.
verdict: The Cebu Marathon is a big, international pre-Sinulog race with a competitive front end, but its 2026 edition was marred by poor finish-line logistics. It drew 11,529 runners from 47 countries on 11 January 2026 [1][2]. SEA Games silver medallist Artjoy Torregosa won the women's marathon in 2:53:17, her first sub-three in Cebu, and Kenya's Eric Chepsiror the men's in 2:30:53 [2]. But medals were not handed out at the finish: runners queued for hours at two booths, a finisher took the microphone at the awards to complain, and police ended up helping distribute medals [3]. One runner also criticised the lack of cramp spray on the course [3]. The organisers had promised a smoother race after similar complaints in 2025 [1]. Enter for the race and the atmosphere, but watch what the organisers change for 2027.

sections.heading: The 2026 Edition
paragraphs: The 18th Cebu Marathon was held on Sunday 11 January 2026 at the South Road Properties, based at SM Seaside City Cebu, with 11,529 runners from 47 countries [1][2]. That was slightly fewer than the 12,275 of 2025 [1].

The half marathon was the most popular distance, with 5,428 entries, and 3,732 entered the full marathon; there were also 10 km and 5 km races [1]. Japan sent the largest foreign contingent, followed by the United States and South Korea [1].

sections.heading: The Front of the Race
paragraphs: Artjoy Torregosa won the women's marathon in 2:53:17, her third straight Cebu title and first sub-three-hour finish there [2]. Eric Chepsiror of Kenya won the men's race in 2:30:53 on his return from an ankle injury, ahead of defending champion Florendo Lapiz [2].
Kenya's Daniel Boiwo won the men's half marathon in 1:09:00, and Michelle Zamora the women's in 1:25:47 [2].

sections.heading: The Medal Problem
paragraphs: The finish was where the 2026 race went wrong. Medals were not given at the finish line; long queues formed for medal claiming after the marathon and half marathon, and some runners waited for hours, told only that medals would be available from 7am [3]. During the awards ceremony a 42 km finisher went on stage and took the microphone to complain, to cheers for him and boos for the organisers, after which police helped hand out medals and the queue moved faster [3].

One half-marathon finisher, Lou Ang, wrote that only two booths were distributing medals for thousands of runners and that nobody at the finish told runners where to go [3]. Another runner, Bryan Liwag, said medics along the course had no cramp spray until a point after 35 km, and said he would not run the race again [3]. The organisers, the Cebu Executives Runners Club, had promised improvements after the 2025 edition drew criticism over post-race food and medal delays [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Maybe. The race itself has a big international field, a strong front of the race and the pre-Sinulog atmosphere, and those are real reasons to go.

But two editions in a row drew complaints about finish-line logistics. Before you commit, look for what the organisers say they will change for 2027, particularly on medal distribution and on-course medical support.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2026 edition, including runners' own comments quoted in the press. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.
